value.body: Electronics & Communication Engineering covers circuits, analog and digital electronics, signals and systems, microprocessors, communication systems, electromagnetics and VLSI. Graduates work on chips, embedded systems and telecom — and many also move into software jobs.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: You choose the branch at counselling, after the entrance exam. JEE Advanced rank is used for IITs; JEE Main rank for NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded institutes — all allotted through JoSAA. State colleges use state counselling with a state CET (EAMCET, MHT-CET, KCET, WBJEE and others) or, in Tamil Nadu (TNEA), Class 12 marks. Private universities may run their own tests. Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics is required.

value.title: At a glance
items: Core electronics jobs (VLSI, embedded, telecom) often expect strong fundamentals and, for chip design, frequently an M.Tech.
A large share of ECE graduates take software jobs; colleges usually allow this in placements.
GATE (EC paper) leads to M.Tech and some PSU / research-organisation jobs; UPSC ESE has an Electronics & Telecom stream.
Common next steps: a job, GATE → M.Tech / PSU, or an MS abroad.
